clue.text: Lift best flipping prize

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run back the other way

blocks.note: to jack a car is to lift it
the top is the best

explanation.surface: Someone collects a prize for the best lift, perhaps at a weightlifting contest, flipping the bar overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reads as a weightlifting move but is the verb for raising a car, and 'flipping' turns only the word for best.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the largest prize in a lottery or gambling game, so it is a kind of prize.

clue.text: Idiot wearing sleeveless jacket

blocks.note: a jerk is a fool
someone dressed in a coat is wearing it

explanation.surface: A fool wanders about in a sleeveless jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like it should put one thing around another, but here it simply supplies the little word for being dressed in something.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting waistcoat-like garment with no arms, historically made of leather.

clue.text: Shy about setter and director producing something amusing

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the others

blocks.note: coy means bashful or shy
the setter refers to themself as me
D is an abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A shy crossword setter teams up with a film director to make something funny.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'setter' usually stands for ME, the person who wrote the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is entertainment designed to make people laugh, so it is a funny thing in general terms.

clue.text: After taking ecstasy she appeared strangely bottom heavy

indicators.note: after something has been taken away it is no longer present, so a letter is removed
something done strangely is done oddly, so the letters come out in an odd new order

blocks.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who took ecstasy looked oddly heavy around the hips afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After taking ecstasy' sounds like drug use, but it means after removing one E from the phrase that follows; the remaining ten letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear-shaped figure is wider at the hips and base than at the top, just like the fruit.

clue.text: Body part in doctor's office

indicators.note: in means inside, so the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A patient's body part is being examined at the GP's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is ignored when reading through the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, the section without head, arms or legs.

clue.text: Uncontrolled sheep gasp

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
to pant is to gasp for breath

explanation.surface: A runaway sheep is out of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: A short three-part clue: definition first, then two everyday synonyms joined end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rampant spreads or grows unchecked, without restraint, like rampant inflation or disease.

clue.text: Act as salesman with grudge

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
to resent is to begrudge

explanation.surface: A salesman pretends with a grudge against someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act as' is the definition; it is easy to read it as the start of 'act as salesman'.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent someone is to stand in for them or speak on their behalf, serving in their role.

clue.text: Coerced servant loudly

indicators.note: something said loudly is heard rather than read, so go by sound

blocks.note: a maid is a female servant

explanation.surface: A servant was forced to shout.
explanation.walkthrough: The servant word and the past tense of the verb sound the same but are spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are made to do something you are forced or compelled to do it.

clue.text: Eagerness of Cyril at a review

indicators.note: a review reworks and revises material, so the letters are reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cyril shows great keenness at a performance review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review' reads as a noun at the end of the surface, but it signals rearrangement of the eight letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity means brisk, cheerful readiness, so it is a synonym for keenness and willingness.

clue.text: Love is almost completely true and certain after time

indicators.note: almost means nearly but not quite, so the final letter is dropped
after means following, so the later material comes behind what precedes it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
real means completely true, cut short by one letter
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A sentimental claim that love is nearly always true and sure, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed word plus the certainty word come after the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a term of endearment for a dearly loved person, as in 'my treasure', like 'my love'.

clue.text: Dance and drink with beau regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: rum is a spirit
first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone dances and has a drink with their boyfriend now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like it describes how often the couple go out, but it picks out the odd letters of the boyfriend word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Cuban origin with a distinctive hip movement.

clue.text: Denounce celebrity accepting help making a comeback

indicators.note: to come back is to return the way you came, so the letters run backwards
to accept something is to take it in, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: repute is fame or renown
aid is help

explanation.surface: A faded celebrity attempting a comeback with some help is publicly condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrity' means fame here, not a famous person, and only the help word goes backwards before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or disown something publicly, close in sense to condemning it.

clue.text: Popular detectives sat incapacitated

blocks.note: something in is fashionable
DIs are detective inspectors
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Well-liked police officers sat about, unable to work.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is the British police rank of detective inspector; 'sat' is meant as sitting for an artist or photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone indisposed is slightly ill and unable to carry out their usual duties.

clue.text: Rankles runner taking in run around ...

indicators.note: to take something in is to absorb it inside, so one piece is enclosed
to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: a ski is a runner that slides over snow, like a sledge runner
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An athlete is annoyed at having to run around, the dots leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it is the long blade under a sledge or the like.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles annoys or vexes someone persistently, and so it irks them.

clue.text: Posh car with new instrument serving drink

blocks.note: a limo is a limousine
N is the abbreviation for new
a cello is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A smart limousine carries a musician with a new instrument who also serves drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces simply line up in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoncello is an Italian lemon liqueur, usually served chilled after a meal.

clue.text: ... till sightseer crashed into vehicle

indicators.note: something crashed is smashed up, so the letters are thrown into disorder
going into something puts it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a tourist drives into a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots link the surface to the clue before; 'till' reads as 'until' but it is the shop's money drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is the machine in a shop that records sales and holds the takings.

clue.text: Applauds quality in ball of ice

blocks.note: to hail someone is to acclaim them
tone is a quality, as of sound

explanation.surface: Someone praises the craftsmanship of an ice sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hailstone is a single pellet of frozen rain that falls in a storm.

clue.text: Mirth of liberal offspring losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means a word drops its first letter

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
daughter, a female child, without its first letter

explanation.surface: A liberal's child gets so amused they lose their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offspring' must be narrowed to a specific child word before it is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth is merriment and amusement expressed by laughing, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Wandering sailor and worker concealing blunder

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman
a worker ant
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A roaming seaman and a labourer try to cover up a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a sailor is often AB and a worker is often ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means departing from the normal course, straying from what is expected, so it matches roaming off course.

clue.text: Britain above changing short form

indicators.note: something changing alters its arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Britain rises above changes to some short form of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters of the two words rearrange exactly into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviation is a shortened version of a word or phrase, such as Dr for Doctor.

clue.text: Assumes America excited about king getting success at last

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round another
at last means at the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the US is America
worked up means excited
R is short for rex, Latin for king
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: America gets worked up about a king finally succeeding.
explanation.walkthrough: R for king comes from the Latin rex; 'excited' gives the short word meaning stirred up, which then goes around the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp a throne is to take it over wrongfully, as one assumes power without the right.

clue.text: Overdose promises to be foul

blocks.note: OD is the abbreviation for overdose
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: An overdose looks set to turn out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: IOU is a written note acknowledging a debt, a promise of payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means extremely unpleasant or repulsive, a near synonym of disgusting and vile.

clue.text: Blood group often reported erroneously at first

indicators.note: at first means at the beginning, so the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone's blood group is often recorded wrongly at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blood group' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits after 'Blood' and the next four words supply their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore is blood that has been shed, especially from a wound, as in a gory scene.

clue.text: East German hurried to keep Iceland excluded

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Ost is German for east
raced means rushed
IS is the international code for Iceland

explanation.surface: An East German rushed to keep Iceland out of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' reads as a person from East Germany, but it is the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ostracised is to be shut out from a group or society, deliberately shunned.

clue.text: Climbs right before noon to get additional note

blocks.note: R is short for right
the hours before noon are a.m.
a PS is a postscript added to a letter

explanation.surface: Someone climbs right before midday to add an extra note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before noon' gives the morning abbreviation, not something placed before another piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramps are slopes leading up from one level to another, so they are inclines one goes up.

clue.text: Old London players returned to capital

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: O is short for old
the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: Veteran London musicians went back to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' means musicians here: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the seat of government of Norway, so it is an example of a national capital city.

clue.text: Commute in coaches lacking one class

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: to coach is to train
Roman numeral for one
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Travelling to work by coach without a first-class ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commute' looks like a daily journey but is the verb meaning to change, as in commuting a sentence; 'coaches' is the verb, not the vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To commute something is to change it into another form, as a death sentence into life imprisonment.

clue.text: Slow Greek vessel following line

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the later piece is placed behind

blocks.note: L is short for line
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A sluggish Greek ship sails behind a line of others.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction meaning to play in a slow and broad tempo.

clue.text: Artist going to crappy hotel gets squalid room

indicators.note: something crappy is in a bad state, so the letters are messed about

blocks.note: an RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist checks into a shabby hotel and is given a filthy room.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A rathole is informal for a dirty, cramped and shabby place to live or stay.

clue.text: Partners returning concessions holding value

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters run the other way
to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: sops are small concessions made to placate someone
use is value, as in 'of no use'

explanation.surface: Husbands and wives come back with concessions that hold some value.
explanation.walkthrough: A sop is something given to pacify, as in a sop to public opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouses are married partners, husbands or wives.
